subject: Private VPC observability: on‑prem collector & SIEM ingest runbook

Subject: On‑prem collector + SIEM mapping for Redwood Private (Acme VPC)

Marcus / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran the POC agent in our staging VPC overnight and have two immediate asks before we approve the production package:

1) A concise runbook for on‑prem collector install that maps to our internal SIEM (Splunk HEC + legacy syslog).
2) Field mapping guidance and sample regex parsers for our security events (authN/authZ, model inference audit events, admin API calls).

Our constraints: no outbound internet egress from the cluster except to an approved forwarder IP; mTLS required between agents and the forwarder; retention for raw events is 365 days, indexed events 7 years.

Can you provide the runbook and a sample collector config we can run in a staging namespace? Also include the expected size (GB/day) ballpark for 2000 inference containers with standard token logging.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Security Engineering, Acme Corp
Acme Security

Subject: Re: On‑prem collector + SIEM mapping for Redwood Private (Acme VPC)

Alex — thanks, this is helpful. I pushed an initial draft runbook and a sample OpenTelemetry collector config for an internal forwarder to the attachments. High level response to your bullets: 

- Runbook: stepwise installer that assumes an internal forwarder (LogiSys) handling egress. Will include firewall rules, serviceaccount and K8s PSP alternatives, cert rotation cadence for mTLS, and validation steps (test events and HEC acknowledgement).

- Field mapping: we created a recommended mapping sheet for Splunk (attached) that maps Redwood fields (request_id, model_id, prompt_digest, token_count, inference_latency_ms, outcome) to Splunk indexed fields. Also added example regex for parsing legacy syslog lines when customers push aggregated proxy messages.

- Size estimate: with token‑level sampling (10% default) and structured JSON logs (no full prompt retention) we estimate ~18–28 GB/day for 2k containers depending on sequence length. If you need full prompt retention at peak lengths the number rises ~3–4x — we'll call that out in the runbook.

Next steps: Kimberly will own the acceptance checklist and Marissa will coordinate the staging run.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: private-obsv-runbook-v1.md (runbook), onprem-collector-config.yaml (OTel collector example), splunk-field-mapping.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Acme Security <secops@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2024 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem collector + SIEM mapping for Redwood Private (Acme VPC)

Alex — quick clarifications and acceptance criteria from the compliance side: 

1) Egress model: we need a single approved forwarder IP/CIDR and an allowlist of ports (TLS 443 + custom HEC port if you run a private HEC endpoint). The runbook includes iptables/CNI policy snippets for Calico and AWS VPC egress rules.

2) mTLS: we recommend short‑lived certs (7d rotation) with an internal CA (HashiVault or customer KMS). Runbook contains batch renewal steps and a fallback policy (grace period + backup key) so agents don't get orphaned during rotation.

3) Tracing hooks: add a low‑overhead span header on inference calls (x-rw-span-id) — we provide a small SDK middleware to emit span ids and sample traces to your tracing collector (Jaeger/Zipkin). We'll keep sampling at 0.1% by default for production and allow you to bump to 1% for rolling debug windows.

4) Oncall and evidence: for any retention/audit questions, include a dedicated evidence bundle exporter (runs weekly) that zips raw events and signed manifests to an S3 compatible bucket behind the forwarder; manifest includes a SHA256 checksum and the runbook lists encryption options.

I'll own the acceptance checklist and will review the staging results next week. Marissa — please schedule the staging window and include the LogiSys team for collector tuning.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference

We reviewed the runbook and the collector config in staging. Quick notes from testing team: 

- Installer script executed cleanly in our isolated namespace.
- mTLS handshake passed with our internal CA but we swapped the cert rotation to 14 days for operational convenience (agree to shorter rotations in a tighter rollout).
- Splunk mapping sheet mapped cleanly; we requested two additional fields: inference_model_version and prompt_redaction_flag (we added comments in the spreadsheet).

LogiSys will tune the batching and drop policy for HEC to avoid backpressure during bursts. We are comfortable to move to a 2‑week production pilot assuming the final mapping and the weekly evidence export are in place.
